messages:
alex_finance: Heads up 1 procurement investigating QuantaLedger vs QuantaLogic for ML billing. Need quick callouts on invoice quirks, meter granularity, and any hidden fees. cc @sasha_procurement @jamie_engineering

sasha_procurement: Do we want to compare committed reserves (Dedicated-like) or pure PAYG? Committed gives discounts but adds commit risk.

jamie_engineering: For context: ~5M gen tokens/mo, ~200k embeddings/mo, bursts at 150 RPS for short windows. Gen ~65% of total token use.

jamie_engineering: Snippet of our hourly profile pasted: ```hourly_qps: 08:00=12, 12:00=88, 18:00=145, 23:00=35```

alex_finance: Audit question: do either vendor round token counts (e.g., up to 1k) or bill exact? Also how do invoices present SKUs (do they show per-model, per-endpoint, per-region breakdown)?

billingbot: Sample invoice links uploaded: QuantaLedger: https://s3.redwood.test/ql-ledger-invoice-feb.pdf ; QuantaLogic: https://s3.redwood.test/ql-logic-invoice-feb.pdf

nora_audit: Quick skim: QuantaLedger lists line items as "model:sku:hour-bucket" which makes reconciliation easier, but shows monthly true-up adjustments that can shift prior lines. Need to confirm their adjustment policy.

sasha_procurement: QuantaLogic offered a 12% discount on a 12-month committed spend and an optional overage cap at 125% for an extra fee. QuantaLedger proposes volume tiers with month-to-month true-ups instead of hard commits.

jamie_engineering: Important nuance: QuantaLedger bills embeddings per API call (flat per-request), QuantaLogic bills per-vector which hurts us if we batch vectors into single requests. Confirm vector->request mapping with vendors.

alex_finance: Can someone do a 6-month back-of-envelope TCO with assumptions: 5M gen tokens/mo, 200k embeddings/mo, 2% monthly growth, include discounts and overage caps? We just need a basic number to guide procurement.

sasha_procurement: On it 1 will build a quick sheet and flag contract items: invoice dispute window (QuantaLedger=30d, QuantaLogic=45d per their quotes), SLA credit mechanics (credit applied as future invoice vs direct refund), audit rights, termination notice.

oliver_legal: Ask legal: do they pass SLA credits as invoice reductions or only as future credits? We prefer invoice reductions for material outages. Also check indemnity and data residency clauses.

billingbot: Vendor reply (QuantaLedger): "We bill exact token counts; hourly aggregation. Adjustments posted as credit memo within 30 days. Embeddings billed per call"

billingbot: Vendor reply (QuantaLogic): "We bill per-vector; rounding to nearest vector (no token rounding). Committed customers get month-to-month price lock and optional overage cap. Invoice adjustments within 45 days"

tina_ops: Note on throttling: both vendors have burst addons. QuantaLogic explicitly offers burst nodes at +20% cost for sustained spikes; QuantaLedger has a soft-throttle policy with paid emergency capacity. Need SLA language.

nora_audit: Add sensitivity: if embeddings billed per-vector vs per-call, effective cost swings +/- 30% for our batched pipelines. Sasha please add a sensitivity row.

sasha_procurement: Uploaded comparison: https://docs.redwood/quanta-tco-draft (I labelled rows: PAYG vs Commit vs Commit+overagecap). Planning follow-up calls Tues.

alex_finance: Great. Paste any vendor confirmations about invoice credits vs future credit, rounding rules, and exact embedding metering here once you have them. Also include whether credits reduce current invoice balance or only apply as account credit. :ok_hand:
